body:
The best Designjoy alternatives are ManyPixels and Penji if you want a cheaper unlimited-request subscription, Design Pickle, DesignMe or Superside if you need a bigger team, and a fixed-scope Ebaq Design Brand Sprint if what you actually need is a brand identity rather than a request queue.

Designjoy itself now costs $4,995 a month (discounted from $5,995) for one request at a time.

I checked every price below on each company's own pricing page on November 20, 2026.

Disclosure: I run Ebaq Design, which is one of the options.

I list it by price like the others, with its real drawback.

Designjoy Alternatives Compared

Sorted from lowest to highest starting price.

OptionPrice (checked Nov 20, 2026)Best for
Designjoy$4,995/moA steady stream of requests
ManyPixelsFrom $699/moEveryday marketing graphics on a budget
PenjiFrom $995/moMarketing teams and agencies
Design PickleFrom $2,200/moSteady weekly demand
Ebaq Design$3,000/week or $10,000/monthA brand identity, rebrand or website
DesignMeFrom $6,000/moFunded startups needing design and development
Superside$15,000/mo minimum, annual termLarge in-house marketing teams

What Designjoy Offers (and Why People Look Elsewhere)

Designjoy popularized design as a subscription when it launched in 2017.

According to its own site, it is run entirely by its founder, Brett, with no extra designers and no outsourcing, and it takes a limited number of clients at a time.

The Monthly Club plan (see Designjoy's pricing) includes one request at a time, an average 48-hour delivery, unlimited brands, Webflow development, stock photos and up to two users.

You can pause or cancel anytime, and if it is not working after a week you get 75% back.

People usually look for alternatives for two reasons: the price, which is close to a senior hire, and the one-at-a-time queue, which slows down when you have many small requests.

What Customers and Critics Say About Designjoy

Independent reviews of Designjoy are thin, so I looked for first-hand accounts and the founder's own public posts.

  • Slow replies and paying for idle months: Failory's founder, who subscribed for one month to redesign his site, wrote that he sometimes waited two to three days to hear back and that you pay the full fee even in months you send no requests. He still rated the work highly, and his review contains affiliate links.
  • How "unlimited" one designer can be: on Hacker News, a contractor did the math on one person serving around 30 subscribers at once and questioned what "unlimited requests" means in practice.
  • Disputes on both sides: Brett has written about a client who filed a chargeback for $5,000 of finished branding and website work, and about a client dispute that, by his count, reached 1.3 million views on X.
  • Doubts about who does the work: he has also responded to claims that Designjoy is a scam staffed by outsourced freelancers, which he denies, and to the criticism that he rarely shows client work.

Most of these complaints come down to two things: one person's capacity and a flat fee you pay whether or not you use it.

Both apply to any design subscription, so check them before you sign up for any service on this list.

1. ManyPixels

Price: $699/mo for up to 2 hours of design a day, $1,199/mo for up to 4 hours, $1,399/mo for an assigned designer and $2,599/mo for a two-designer team. See the ManyPixels pricing page.

Every plan includes unlimited requests and revisions, unlimited brands, a project manager, stock assets and full IP transfer.

Delivery is next-day on the shared plans and same-day with an assigned designer.

Drawback: the cheaper plans are capped by hours of design a day, so "unlimited" requests still move at the speed of those hours.

Best for: social posts, ads, decks and landing pages for a team that already knows what it wants.

2. Penji

Price: $995/mo (Essentials), $1,995/mo (Agency Partner) and $4,500/mo (Dedicated Team). See the Penji pricing page.

Essentials covers two active projects with a one-business-day turnaround and a project manager.

Agency Partner adds a third active project, same-day turnaround, an art director, motion graphics and short-form video.

Penji offers a 30-day money-back guarantee and no contracts.

Drawback: motion and video start at the $1,995 plan, and senior-only creatives and front-end development come only with the $4,500 plan.

Best for: marketing teams and agencies with a steady flow of campaign assets.

3. Design Pickle

Price: from $2,200/mo, billed monthly, with savings on quarterly or annual terms. See the Design Pickle pricing page.

You are priced by design time per day and keep the same creatives every time, with an art director and coordinator overseeing the work.

The plan covers up to three brands and includes social, ads, decks, video, motion, web and email.

Drawback: $2,200 is a starting figure: the real price depends on how much daily design time you build, and crews above six hours a day need a quarterly or annual term.

Best for: companies with steady weekly demand that want the same team every time.

4. Ebaq Design Brand Sprint

Price: $3,000 flat for one week, or $10,000 for a month booked upfront. See the Ebaq Design pricing page.

This is my studio, and you work directly with me rather than with an account manager or a queue.

One week covers a complete brand identity or rebrand: several logo concepts, revisions within the agreed scope, final logo files, logo animation, color palette, typography, brand guidelines, business cards, social profile images and launch posts, and an email signature.

Further weeks at the same rate cover motion and launch assets, website design in Figma, and development in Framer, Webflow or Next.js.

See the Brand Sprint or the monthly option for details.

Drawback: it is one senior designer and a fixed scope, not an open queue, so you can't drop in twenty ad resizes on a Tuesday, and you pay for the week upfront.

Best for: a startup or growing company that needs its brand done properly once, then a website.

5. DesignMe

Price: $6,000/mo for the Design plan, $8,000/mo for Development and $12,000/mo for Design + Development; one-off projects such as a brand identity sprint start at $10,000. See the DesignMe pricing page.

The Design plan gives you a senior team working on one active request at a time, with an unlimited backlog, billed monthly with the option to pause or cancel.

Design + Development runs two requests at once, one in design and one in build, so designs ship as working code.

Teams backed by YC, a16z or a similar fund get 10% off monthly plans.

Drawback: the Design plan is still one request at a time, like Designjoy, but costs about $1,000 more a month, and its brand identity sprint takes up to four weeks from $10,000.

Best for: funded startups that want brand, website and product design and development from one senior team.

6. Superside

Price: subscriptions start at a $15,000 monthly minimum on an annual term. See the Superside pricing page.

Superside offers a dedicated team, a flexible plan with budget that rolls over month to month, and fixed-scope projects.

Every subscription includes senior creatives, creative strategy, unlimited users and its own project platform.

Drawback: the minimum is about three times Designjoy's monthly price and needs a twelve-month commitment.

Best for: in-house marketing teams at larger companies with constant creative demand.

If none of these fit, the other route is a traditional agency.

In my experience, agency proposals for a full identity run $25k–$100k+ over 3–9 months.

For a broader price map, see my guide on logo design and branding cost.

Subscription or Fixed Scope: How to Choose

Design subscriptions are built for a queue of known requests: an ad, a deck, a landing page.

A brand identity is a different kind of job: a series of decisions about positioning, logo and system that have to be made in order.

When a new brand goes through a request queue, each request gets designed without the strategy behind it, and you end up art-directing the brand yourself.

My rule of thumb:

  • If you can write the request in one sentence, use a subscription.
  • If you need someone to decide what the brand should be, book fixed-scope work with a senior designer first, then hand the guidelines to a subscription for day-to-day assets.

That combination is often cheaper than either option alone.

Here is an example over three months, using the prices above:

PlanFirst three months
Designjoy for three months3 × $4,995 = $14,985
Brand Sprint, then Penji Essentials for three months$3,000 + 3 × $995 = $5,985
Brand Sprint, then ManyPixels Advanced for three months$3,000 + 3 × $699 = $5,097

The cheaper plans give you fewer design hours a day than a dedicated senior designer, so compare the volume you actually need, not only the price.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Designjoy worth it?

If you have a steady flow of requests and like working with one experienced designer, yes.

At $4,995 a month, though, it is priced like a senior hire, not a budget service.

What is the cheapest Designjoy alternative?

Of the services I checked, ManyPixels starts lowest at $699 a month, for up to two hours of design a day.

Can a design subscription do my branding?

Most of them list logos and branding, and they can produce the files.

What a request queue rarely gives you is the strategy and the decisions behind a brand, which is why I recommend fixed-scope work for the identity itself.

Does Designjoy build websites?

Yes: Webflow development is included in its Monthly Club plan.

Conclusion

For ongoing marketing graphics, ManyPixels, Penji and Design Pickle cost less than Designjoy, and Superside is the step up for large teams.

For a new brand or a rebrand, a fixed-scope week with a senior designer is usually the better first move.

If that is where you are, book a call and we can work out which one fits.
